messages:
pagerduty: :rotating_light: INCIDENT INC-2026-0341 — Elevated 5xx / timeouts observed on /v1/generate across us-east-1. Alert thresholds breached (5xx rate > 5% sustained). Paging oncall: maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): oncall here, seeing the page. Pulling up metrics now. :eyes:

sam (sre): initial look — Grafana shows scheduler queue length spiking ~11:12 UTC, average queue latency up to 6s, and a corresponding bump in gateway 504s. Looks like batching/scheduler saturation + head-of-line blocking.

jin (runtime): confirming — batcher logs show long-running batches waiting on KV cache fetch for a subset of requests (model=redwood-xxl-q4). Some requests open huge sequences, blocking downstream.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce batch size to break up large head-of-line batches; 2) spin up extra scheduler workers; 3) enable fallback model variant for high-latency requests; 4) temporarily increase gateway timeouts to avoid upstream cascading. Will coordinate.

sam (sre): agreed. Commands I'm about to run:
```
# scale scheduler workers
kubectl scale deployment scheduler-workers -n inference --replicas=8
# reduce batch size config (applies dynamically)
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' https://control-plane/api/v1/configs/batcher -d '{"max_batch_tokens":1024, "max_batch_size":8}'
```

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by sam: rollout scheduler-workers -> replicas=8 (job id: deploy-2026-03-05-419).

jin (runtime): also toggling model fallback policy. New policy: if queue latency > 2s then route to redwood-xxl-q4-fallback (quantized) for non-high-priority requests. Pushing rule now.

maya (oncall): applying routing rule: `policy.apply('fallback-on-queue', threshold=2s, target='redwood-xxl-q4-fallback')` — applied.

carlos (support): quick note — Support is seeing customer-reported timeouts (enterprise-account-42, streaming partner). Drafting a customer-facing incident note. Priority: high.

sam (sre): after scaling & batcher config change, queue length dropped ~40% within 60s, 5xx rate trending down but some 504 spikes remain. Looks like head-of-line blocking improved.

jin (runtime): logs show a subset of requests still causing long CPU/GPU work (long context lengths). I've added a request-router filter to deprioritize requests with context > 20k tokens to background queue.

maya (oncall): adding short-term guardrail: increase gateway timeout from 10s -> 20s to avoid premature 504s while mitigation stabilizes. Applying now.

sam (sre): note — increasing gateway timeout may increase client-perceived latency but reduces 504 churn. We'll revert when stable.

echo-bot: metric check: 5xx rate current: 1.8% (was 6.5% at peak). median p95 latency: 240ms -> 400ms.

maya (oncall): good progress. Next steps: 1) keep scheduler replicas at 8 for 30m then re-evaluate autoscaler thresholds; 2) run targeted evictions for very long requests; 3) enable per-route fallback for top-10 customers if they keep timing out.

carlos (support): I'm preparing a short support update for affected customers, ETA 15m. Who can confirm customer list?

sam (sre): query: `select customer_id, count(*) as timeouts from gateway_logs where code in (502,504) group by customer_id order by timeouts desc limit 50` — I'll paste results into incident doc in 2m.

maya (oncall): handoff note — I will stay with this incident for next 25 minutes then hand to sam for night watch. Leaving runbook entry in INC-2026-0341.

jin (runtime): adding extra tracing for batcher path to capture sample request that triggers longest wait. If we can repro, we'll create a regression test.

sam (sre): monitoring — set alert threshold: if 5xx > 2% for 5m, notify oncall escalation. Also created a temporary Grafana dash for this incident.

deploy-bot: scheduler-workers scaled to 8 — pods ready: 8/8.

maya (oncall): after mitigation: observed error rate dropped and tail latency improving. Requesting postmortem and follow-ups:
- root cause hypothesis: batching scheduler saturation due to a mix of a spike in very long-context requests + inflexible batching parameters leading to head-of-line blocking.
- action items: add per-request size caps, smarter preemptive batching (split oversized requests), improve autoscaling thresholds for scheduler based on queue length and token throughput, add more robust fallback routing for model hotspots.

carlos (support): support update sent to affected customers. No escalations right now.

maya (oncall): closing the active paging loop — we'll keep the incident open for postmortem. Sam will take over monitoring. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sam (sre): taking over monitoring. Filing INC-2026-0341 postmortem placeholder.
